proposals.before: 1. Let us recall the Riemann-Roch formula for a proper morphism \[f\colon X \to Y\] of schemes quasi-projective and smooth over a field \(k\), and a coherent sheaf \(F\) on \(X\), whose class in the group \(K(X)\) of classes of coherent sheaves on \(X\) is denoted by \(c\ell(F)\): \[\operatorname{Todd}(T_Y)\, \operatorname{ch}_Y(f_*(c\ell(F))) = f_*(\operatorname{Todd}(T_X)\, \operatorname{ch}_X(F)) \tag{1.1}\] This formula is valid in \(A(Y)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}\), where \(A(Y)\) is the Chow ring of \(Y\), the \(f_*\) of the right-hand side being deduced by tensoring with \(\mathbb{Q}\) from the "direct image of cycles" homomorphism \[f_*\colon A(X) \to A(Y) ,\] that of the left-hand side being the Euler-Poincaré characteristic of \(F\) relative to \(f\): \[f_*(c\ell(F)) = \sum_i (-1)^i c\ell(R^i f_*(F)) ;\] \(\operatorname{ch}_X\), \(\operatorname{ch}_Y\) denote the Chern characters on \(X\) resp. on \(Y\), and \(T_X,T_Y\) the tangent bundles of \(X\) resp. of \(Y\). As is well known, \(\operatorname{Todd}(-)\) and \(\operatorname{ch}(-)\) are universal polynomials with coefficients in \(\mathbb{Q}\) in the Chern classes of the argument. The constant term of \(\operatorname{Todd}(-)\) being \(1\), it is an invertible element for every value of the argument, so that formula (1.1) takes, after multiplication by \(\operatorname{Todd}(T_Y)^{-1}\), the equivalent form, more convenient for our purpose \[\operatorname{ch}_Y(f_*(c\ell(F))) = f_*(\operatorname{Todd}(T_f)\cdot\operatorname{ch}_X(F)) , \tag{1.2}\] where we have set \[T_f = T_X - f^*(T_Y) \in K(X) , \tag{1.3}\] so that \(T_f\) plays the role of a virtual relative tangent bundle of \(X\) over \(Y\). In the case where the morphism \(f\) is smooth (i.e. with tangent map everywhere surjective), we have simply \[T_f = T_{X/Y} \quad \text{(fibré tangent le long des fibres)} ,\] while in the case where \(f\colon X \to Y\) is an immersion, one finds \[T_f = -\check{N}_{X/Y} ,\] where \(\check{N}_{X/Y}\) denotes the normal sheaf of \(X\) in \(Y\).

proposals.before: When one considers schemes \(X\) proper over a field, the projection \[f^X\colon X \to (\mathrm{point})\] defines an "Euler-Poincaré characteristic" homomorphism \[\chi_X = f_*^X\colon K_{\bullet}(X) \to K_{\bullet}(\mathrm{point}) = \mathbb{Z} , \tag{6.4}\] inducing on the subgroup \(\operatorname{Gr}_0(X) = \operatorname{Filt}_0 K_{\bullet}(X)\) the "degree of 0-cycles" homomorphism \[\deg_X\colon \operatorname{Gr}_0(X) \to \mathbb{Z} . \tag{6.5}\] The multiplication homomorphism \[\operatorname{Gr}^i(X) \times \operatorname{Gr}_i(X) \to \operatorname{Gr}_0(X) ,\] composed with the degree homomorphism (6.5), then provides a pairing \[\operatorname{Gr}^i(X) \times \operatorname{Gr}_i(X) \to \mathbb{Z} , \tag{6.6}\] which explains why in certain respects \(\operatorname{Gr}'(X)\) and \(\operatorname{Gr}_{\bullet}(X)\) play dual roles, just like cohomology and homology. Thus, if \(f\colon X \to Y\) is a morphism of proper algebraic schemes, the two homomorphisms \[f^*\colon \operatorname{Gr}'(Y) \to \operatorname{Gr}'(X) \quad \text{et} \quad f_*\colon \operatorname{Gr}_{\bullet}(X) \to \operatorname{Gr}_{\bullet}(Y)\] are formally transposes of each other, in the sense of the pairings (6.6).

\[A_S^p\longrightarrow A_S^q\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow0,\]

Then we have:

\[ \mathrm{a)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{a')} \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{b)}\Longleftarrow\mathrm{b')}. \]

\[ (**)\qquad E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M \longrightarrow\mathbf R\!\operatorname{Hom}(E^\vee,M). \]

\[ (***)\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^{p+1}(E^\vee,M) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H^{-p-1}(E^\vee),M), \]

\[ \mathrm{a')}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{a)} \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{b)} \Longleftarrow\mathrm{b')} \]

For the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)})\), we may assume \(E^1=0\), i.e. replace \(E\) by \(E'=(0\longrightarrow E^{-1}\longrightarrow E^0\longrightarrow0)\). We already know that the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^0(E'_{k(x)})\) is upper semi-continuous, hence so is the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E'_{k(x)})=\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)})\), since the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^0(E'_{k(x)})-\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E'_{k(x)})=\operatorname{rg}(E'_x)\) is locally constant.

Let us now prove the second assertion. After truncating, we may assume \(E\) strictly perfect and \(E^i=0\) for \(i<p-1\). The \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module \(Z'^i(E)=\operatorname{Coker}(E^{i-1}\longrightarrow E^i)\) is therefore of finite presentation. We have an exact sequence:

\[ (*)\qquad 0\longrightarrow H^p(E)\longrightarrow Z'^p(E)\longrightarrow E^{p+1} \longrightarrow Z'^{p+1}(E)\longrightarrow0. \]

Since the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) is right and left exact, \(Z'^{p+1}(E)\) and \(Z'^p(E)\) are flat by (5.2 (iii)), hence (I 5.8.3) locally free of finite type. The exactness of \((*)\) then implies that \(H^p(E)\) is locally free of finite type, and consequently that the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^p(E_{k(x)})=\operatorname{rg}(H^p(E)_x)\)

is locally constant, which completes the proof of (ii).

(iii) We may assume \(E\) strictly perfect and \(E^i=0\) for \(i<p\) (resp. \(p-1\)). To say that the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}M)\) is right exact (resp. left exact) on \(\operatorname{Mod}(x)\) is equivalent, by (5.2 (iii)), to saying that \(Z'^{p+1}(E_x)\) (resp. \(Z'^p(E_x)\)) (with the notations of (ii)) is flat, hence free of finite type (being of finite presentation). Since we have \(Z'^{p+1}(E_x)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}Z'^{p+1}(E)_x\) (resp. \(Z'^p(E_x)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}Z'^p(E)_x\)), the usual argument (cf. EGA \(0_{\mathrm I}\) 5.2.7) shows that there exists a \(x\)-pointed object \(U\) of \(X\) such that \(Z'^{p+1}(E|U)\) (resp. \(Z'^p(E|U)\)) is free of finite type, and we are done.

Corollary 5.6. (EGA III 7.6.9).

Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(p\in\mathbb Z\), and \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\) a \((p-1)\)-pseudo-coherent complex. Then:

(i) For \(x\in X\), \(H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(x))\) is of finite rank over \(k(x)\) and the function

\[ x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(x)) \]

is constructible and upper semi-continuous on \(X\).

(ii) Suppose \(X\) quasi-separated and \(E\) with quasi-coherent and locally bounded cohomology. If the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) is exact on the category of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules, the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(x))\) is locally constant and \(H^p(E)\) is locally free of finite type. Conversely, if \(X\) is locally noetherian and reduced and if the preceding function is locally constant, the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) is exact on the category of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules.

Proof. If \(X\) is integral with generic point \(x\), the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}M)\) is exact on the category of \(\mathcal O_{X,x}\)-modules (since \(\mathcal O_{X,x}=k(x)\)), hence (5.5 (iii)), there exists an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\) such that the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E|U\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) is exact on \(\operatorname{Mod}(U)\), and, on \(U\), the function

\[ y\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(y)) \]

is locally constant by (5.5 (ii)). The constructibility assertion of (i) follows at once. The other assertions follow from (5.5 (ii) and (iii)) and (5.2 (iv)), except the converse of (ii), for which it suffices, after reducing to \(E\) strictly perfect (after localization and truncation), to apply (EGA III 7.6.2 and 7.6.5) to the functor \(T_{-p}=H^p(E\otimes\,\cdot\,)\).

Proposition 5.7. (EGA III 7.7.5 et 7.9.4).

Let \(f:X\longrightarrow Y\) be a proper morphism of quasi-compact schemes, \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^b(f)_{\mathrm{parf}}\) (4.2), and \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Then, subject to the validity of (2.1), hence for example if \(f\) is projective or if \(Y\) is noetherian:

(i) For \(y\in Y\), the \(H^i(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y))\) are vector spaces of finite rank over \(k(y)\), zero except for a finite number, and the function

\[ y\longmapsto\sum(-1)^i\operatorname{rg}_{k(y)} H^i(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y)) \]

is locally constant on \(Y\).

(ii) The function

\[ y\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(y)} H^p(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y)) \]

is constructible and upper semi-continuous on \(Y\).

(iii) Suppose \(Y\) quasi-separated. Then, if the functor \(M\longmapsto R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) is exact on the category of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Modules, \(R^pf_*(E)\) is a locally free \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Module of finite type, and the function of (ii) is locally constant. Conversely, if \(Y\) is noetherian and reduced, and if the function of (ii) is locally constant, the functor \(M\longmapsto R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) is exact on the category of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Modules.

Proof. By (4.8), \(Rf_*(E)\) is a perfect complex. Assertion (i) (resp. (ii)) thus follows from (5.5 (i)) (resp. (5.6 (i))). Finally, if \(M\) is a quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Module, the canonical arrow

\[ Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M \longrightarrow Rf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \]

is an isomorphism by (3.7), so assertion (iii) follows from (5.6 (ii)).

Remarks 5.8.

a) In the situation of (5.7), let us denote by \(i_y:X_y\longrightarrow X\) the injection of the fiber of \(X\) above a point \(y\) of \(Y\). One can show (cf. (EGA III 6 and IV 3.1.0)) that for \(f\) flat (resp. \(E\) bounded with quasi-coherent and \(Y\)-flat components) we have the Künneth formula:

\[ H^i(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y)) \mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}H^i(X_y,E_y), \]

where \(E_y=Li_y^*(E)\) (resp. \(i_y^*(E)\)).

b) One can develop for complex analytic spaces an apparatus analogous to that of this section (exchange, semi-continuity and continuity properties)(1). The essential ingredients are: 1) the finiteness theorem for proper morphisms ("Grauert's theorem"); 2) an analogue of the projection formula (3.7), which can be stated as follows: let \(f:X\longrightarrow Y\) be a morphism of analytic spaces, where \(X\) is assumed to be of bounded dimension, and let \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\), \(M\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(Y)_{\mathrm{coh}}\) ("coh" means "with coherent cohomology"). The canonical arrow

\[ Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M \longrightarrow Rf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \]

is an isomorphism (the hypothesis on \(X\) ensures (T.F II 5.12) that \(f_*\) is of finite cohomological dimension, hence that \(Rf_*\) is defined on \(D(X)\)).

Unlike statement 1), statement 2) is essentially trivial, and follows from a dévissage analogous to that of the proof of (3.7); one has moreover more elbow room since \(Rf_*\) is defined on \(D(X)\), in particular no hypothesis on \(E\) is needed (apart from \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\)).

BIBLIOGRAPHY

[1] Grauert, H., Ein Theorem der Analytischen Garbentheorie ..., Pub. IHES, n°5.

[H] Hartshorne, R., Residues and Duality, Lecture Notes n°20, Springer, 1966.

[T.F] Godement, R., Théorie des faisceaux, Hermann, 1958.

5. Applications: exchange and semi-continuity theorems(1).

Lemma 5.1.

Let \((X,\mathcal O_X)\) be a (commutative) ringed topos, let us denote by \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) the category of \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules, \(D(X)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(X))\). Let \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\), and \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Consider the following conditions:

a) The functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) from \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) to \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) is right exact.

a') The canonical arrow

\[ H^p(E)\otimes M\longrightarrow H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M) \]

is an isomorphism for every \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Mod}(X)\).

b) The functor \(M\longmapsto H^{p+1}(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) from \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) to \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) is left exact.

b') The canonical arrow defined below

\[ (*)\qquad H^{p+1}(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(H^{-p-1}(E^\vee),M) \]

is an isomorphism for every \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Mod}(X)\).

Then we have:

\[ \mathrm{a)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{a')} \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{b)}\Longleftarrow\mathrm{b')}. \]

Moreover, if \(E\) is pseudo-coherent, the conditions a), a'), b), b') are equivalent.

Definition of \((*)\). The canonical arrow (I 7.5) \(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}E\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X\), where \(E^\vee=\mathbf R\!\operatorname{Hom}(E,\mathcal O_X)\), gives, by tensoring with \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Mod}(X)\), an arrow

\[ E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}E \mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M\longrightarrow M, \]

whence, by the adjunction formula dear to Cartan (I 7.4), a canonical arrow

\[ (**)\qquad E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M \longrightarrow\mathbf R\!\operatorname{Hom}(E^\vee,M). \]

Composing the arrow induced by \((**)\) on \(H^{p+1}\) with the canonical arrow

\[ (***)\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^{p+1}(E^\vee,M) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H^{-p-1}(E^\vee),M), \]

we obtain the arrow \((*)\).

Proof. The implications

\[ \mathrm{a')}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{a)} \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{b)} \Longleftarrow\mathrm{b')} \]

are trivial. Let us prove a) \(\Longrightarrow\) a'). Let \(M\) be a \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module. There exists an exact sequence \(M^1\longrightarrow M^0\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow0\), where \(M^0\) and \(M^1\) are direct sums of sheaves of the type \(\mathcal O_{U,X}\), where \(U\) is an object of \(X\). Using the right exactness and the commutation with direct sums of the functors \(H^p(E)\otimes\,\cdot\,\) and \(H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}\,\cdot\,)\), we are reduced to proving that the arrow of a') is an isomorphism for \(M=\mathcal O_{U,X}\), \(U\in\operatorname{ob}X\). Now \(H^p(E)\otimes\mathcal O_{U,X}\) (resp. \(H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}\mathcal O_{U,X})\)) is canonically identified (SGA 4 IV 2.13) with \(i_!(H^p(E)|U)\) (resp. \(H^p(i_!(E|U))\)), where \(i_!\) is the extension by \(0\) outside \(U\), and we are done because \(i_!\) is exact.

Suppose \(E\) pseudo-coherent, and let us prove b) \(\Longrightarrow\) b'). It obviously suffices to show that \((*)\) is an isomorphism for \(M\) injective. Since the arrow \((***)\) is an isomorphism for \(M\) injective, the assertion will thus follow from the following one:

(5.1.1): the arrow \((**)\) is an isomorphism if \(E\) is pseudo-coherent and \(M\) injective.

Proof of (5.1.1). Let us denote by \(T\) (resp. \(T'\)) the functor from \(D^-(X)\) to \(D(X)\) defined by \(F\longmapsto F\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M\) (resp. \(\mathbf R\!\operatorname{Hom}(F^\vee,M)\)). Let \(n\in\mathbb Z\); if \(H^i(F)=0\) for \(i>n\), then \(H^iT(F)=0\) for \(i>n\), \(H^i(F^\vee)=0\) for \(i<-n\), and \(H^iT'(F)=0\) for \(i>n\) if \(M\) is injective. Since on the other hand the arrow \((**)\) commutes with restriction to an open object, and since an injective restricted to an open object is again injective, we may, after localizing and truncating, assume \(E\) strictly perfect (2.1). By dévissage, we then reduce to \(E=\mathcal O_X\), and we are done.

Remarks 5.2.

(i) Condition a) (resp. a'), b), b')) is of a local nature: if \((X_\alpha)\) is an open covering of the final object of \(X\), and if, for each \(\alpha\), condition a) (resp. ...) is satisfied for \(X_\alpha\) and \(E|X_\alpha\), then a) (resp. ...) is satisfied.

(ii) If \(x\) is a point of \(X\), let us denote by \(\mathrm a_x\) (resp. \(\mathrm a'_x\), etc.) the condition a) (resp. a'), etc.) relative to \(E_x\) and \(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{X,x})\). Then, if \(X\) has enough points, condition a) (resp. a'), b)) is equivalent to the condition "for every point \(x\) of \(X\), \(\mathrm a_x\) (resp. \(\mathrm a'_x\), \(\mathrm b_x\))", and is equivalent to the condition "for every point \(x\) of \(X\), \(\mathrm b'_x\)" if \(E\) is pseudo-coherent; moreover condition a') is equivalent to the analogous condition where one replaces "for every \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Mod}(X)\)" by "for every \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module which is the cokernel of a homomorphism \(\mathcal O_{U,X}^p\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{U,X}^q\), where \(U\) is an object of \(X\)".

(iii) The criterion (EGA III 7.4.2) extends word for word to our situation: if \(E\) has flat components, condition a) simply means that \(\operatorname{Coker}(E^p\longrightarrow E^{p+1})\) is flat, hence locally a direct factor of a free Module of finite type if \(E^p\) and \(E^{p+1}\) are moreover assumed to be of finite presentation (I 5.8.3). We deduce from this in particular that, if \(E\) is perfect, then \(E\) satisfies condition a) relative to the integer \(p\) if and only if \(E^\vee\) satisfies condition a) relative to the integer \(-p-1\).

(iv) Let \(X\) be a quasi-separated scheme, \(\mathcal O_X\) the structure sheaf, \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\) a complex with locally bounded and quasi-coherent cohomology. Let us denote by \(\mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\) (resp. \(\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), etc.) the condition analogous to a) (resp. a'), etc.) where one replaces \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) by the category \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(X)\) of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules. Then we have

\[ \mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm b_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftarrow\mathrm b'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}), \]

and the preceding conditions are equivalent if \(E\) is pseudo-coherent.

Indeed, since \(X\) is quasi-separated, every quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine open subset of \(X\) is induced by a quasi-coherent sheaf on \(X\) (EGA I 9.4.2 and IV 1.2.7). It follows that condition \(\mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\) (resp. \(\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), \(\mathrm b_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), \(\mathrm b'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\)) is satisfied if and only if it is satisfied above every affine open subset. To prove the implications above, we may therefore assume \(X\) affine. Then (II 3.5) \(E\) is isomorphic in \(D(X)\) to a complex of quasi-coherent Modules, and the implications

\[ \mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm b_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftarrow\mathrm b'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \]

follow from (5.1) applied to the "punctual" topos ringed by \(\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\); the same holds, by virtue of (II 2.2.10 a)), for the implication \(\mathrm b_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm b'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\) for \(E\) pseudo-coherent. Finally, the equivalence \(\mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), or, what amounts to the same, \(\mathrm a')\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), follows from the last remark of (ii) (and from the fact that quasi-coherent sheaves "extend", \(X\) being quasi-separated).

Proposition 5.3. (exchange property) (EGA III 7.7.5 II).

Let \(f:X\longrightarrow Y\) be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^b(X)\) a complex with quasi-coherent cohomology and of finite flat amplitude rel. to \(f\), and \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Consider the following conditions:

a) The functor \(M\longmapsto R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) from \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\)(1) to \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\)(2) is right exact.

a') The canonical arrow

\[ R^pf_*(E)\otimes M\longrightarrow R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \]

(composed of the canonical arrow \(R^pf_*(E)\otimes M\longrightarrow H^p(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) and of the isomorphism (3.7) \(H^p(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\)) is an isomorphism for every \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\).

b) The functor \(M\longmapsto R^{p+1}f_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) from \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\) to \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\) is left exact.

b') The canonical arrow

\[ R^{p+1}f_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(H^{-p-1}((Rf_*(E))^\vee),M) \]

(composed of the isomorphism (3.7) \(R^{p+1}f_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}H^{p+1}(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) and of the canonical arrow (5.1 \((*)\)) \(H^{p+1}(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H^{-p-1}((Rf_*(E))^\vee),M)\)) is an isomorphism for every \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\).

c) For every base change \(Y'\longrightarrow Y\), the canonical arrow

\[ R^pf_*(E)\otimes_Y\mathcal O_{Y'} \longrightarrow H^p\bigl(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}\mathcal O_{Y'}\bigr) \]

is an isomorphism.

Then we have:

\[ \mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a') \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm b) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm c) \Longleftarrow\mathrm b'). \]

Moreover, if \(f\) is proper, \(E\) pseudo-coherent rel. to \(f\) (hence perfect rel. to \(f\)), and subject to the validity of (2.1) for \(f\) (hence in particular if \(f\) is projective or if \(Y\) is noetherian), the preceding conditions are equivalent.

Proof. The implications \(\mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a')\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm b)\Longleftarrow\mathrm b')\) follow at once from (3.7), (5.1) and (5.2 (iv)), as does the implication \(\mathrm b')\Longleftarrow\mathrm b)\) (for \(f\) proper and \(E\) pseudo-coherent rel. to \(f\)) by virtue of (2.1). It remains to prove that we have \(\mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm c)\). This will follow from the first assertion of the following lemma:

Lemma 5.3.1.

Let \(X\) be a quasi-separated scheme, and let \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\) be a complex with locally bounded and quasi-coherent cohomology. Then condition (5.1 a)) is equivalent to the condition

c) For every scheme \(X'\) over \(X\), the canonical arrow

\[ H^p(E)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'} \longrightarrow H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'}) \]

is an isomorphism.

Moreover, if \(E\) is pseudo-coherent, condition (5.1 a)) implies that, for every morphism \(X'\longrightarrow X\), the canonical arrow

\[ \tag{5.3.1.1} H^{-p-1}(E^\vee)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'} \longrightarrow H^{-p-1}\bigl((E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})^\vee\bigr), \]

composed of \(H^{-p-1}(E^\vee)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'}\longrightarrow H^{-p-1}(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})\) and of the canonical arrow (I 7.1.2) \(H^{-p-1}(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})\longrightarrow H^{-p-1}((E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})^\vee)\), is an isomorphism.

Proof. a) \(\Longrightarrow\) c). The question being local on \(X'\), we may assume \(X\) (resp. \(X'\)) affine with ring \(A\) (resp. \(A'\)). By (II 3.5), we may assume on the other hand that we have \(E=F^\sim\), where \(F\) is a complex of \(A\)-modules. By hypothesis (condition a')) the arrow

\[ H^p(F)\otimes_AA'\longrightarrow H^p(F\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_A}A') \]

is an isomorphism, and we are done since \(H^p(E)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'}\) (resp. \(H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})\)) is canonically identified with the sheaf on \(X'\) defined by the \(A'\)-module \(H^p(F)\otimes_AA'\) (resp. \(H^p(F\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_A}A')\)).

c) \(\Longrightarrow\) a). Taking (5.2 (iv)) into account, it suffices to prove c) \(\Longrightarrow\) \(\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\). The question being local (since \(X\) is quasi-separated), we may assume \(X\) affine with ring \(A\), and \(E=F^\sim\), where \(F\) is a complex of \(A\)-modules. Let \(M=N^\sim\) be a quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module. We must show that the arrow

\[ H^p(F)\otimes_AN\longrightarrow H^p(F\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_A}N) \]

is an isomorphism. But, if we set \(A'=D_A(N)\) (EGA \(0_{\mathrm{IV}}\) 18.2.3), \(X'=\operatorname{Spec}(A')\), this follows from c) applied to the canonical morphism \(X'\longrightarrow X\).

Let us prove the last assertion. The question being local on \(X'\), we may, by (II 2.2.10 b)), assume \(E\) strictly pseudo-coherent. Moreover, since the assertion involves only a part of bounded length of \(E\), we may, after truncating, assume \(E\) strictly perfect. Then \((E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})^\vee\) is canonically identified (I 7.1.2) with \(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'}\), and the arrow (5.3.1.1) can be rewritten as the canonical arrow

\[ (*)\qquad H^{-p-1}(E^\vee)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'} \longrightarrow H^{-p-1}(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'}). \]

If \(E\) satisfies condition (5.1 a)) for the integer \(p\), \(E^\vee\) satisfies the same condition for the integer \(-p-1\) by virtue of (5.2 (iii)), and the arrow \((*)\) is an isomorphism, by the first assertion of (5.3.1). This completes the proof of (5.3.1), and consequently of (5.3).

Remark 5.3.2.

Proposition (5.3) applies in particular when \(E\) is a complex in bounded degrees of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules which are flat and of finite presentation rel. to \(f\): indeed, \(E\) is then of finite perfect amplitude rel. to \(f\) by virtue of (4.3.2).

Definition 5.4.

Let \(X\) be a topos, and let us denote by \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\) the set of its points (SGA 4 IV 6.1). Let \(M\) be an ordered set, \(f:\operatorname{Pt}(X)\longrightarrow M\) a map, and \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\). We say that \(f\) is upper semi-continuous (resp. lower semi-continuous, resp. locally constant) at \(x\) if there exists a \(x\)-pointed object \(U\) of \(X\) such that for every point \(y\) of \(U\) we have \(f(y)\leq f(x)\) (resp. \(f(y)\geq f(x)\), resp. \(f(y)=f(x)\)). We say that \(f\) is upper semi-continuous (resp. lower semi-continuous, resp. locally constant) if it is so at every point(1).

Examples 5.4.1.

a) Let us denote by \(M_X\) the constant sheaf with value \(M\) on \(X\), and let \(s\in H^0(X,M)\). The map \(x\longmapsto s(x)=x^*(s)\) from \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\) to \(M\) is locally constant. In particular, let \(E\) be a perfect complex on \(X\) assumed locally ringed: the rank of \(E\) (I 6.11) defines a locally constant function on \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\) with values in \(\mathbb Z\).

b) Suppose \(X\) locally ringed, and let \(P\) be a \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module of finite type. For \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), let us denote by \(\mathcal O_{X,x}\) the stalk local ring of \(\mathcal O_X\) at \(x\), and by \(k(x)\) the residue field. Then, for \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), \(P_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}k(x)\) is of finite rank over \(k(x)\), and the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}(P_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}k(x))\) is upper semi-continuous. Indeed, if, for \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), \(P_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}k(x)\) is of rank \(n\), there exists an epimorphism \(\mathcal O_{X,x}^n\longrightarrow P_x\) by Nakayama, and, since \(P\) is of finite type, there exists a \(x\)-pointed object \(U\) of \(X\) and an epimorphism \(\mathcal O_U^n\longrightarrow P|U\), whence the assertion.

Lemma 5.5.

Let \((X,\mathcal O_X)\) be a locally ringed topos, \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\), and \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Then, with the notations of (5.4.1 b)), we have:

(i) If \(E\) is perfect, the \(H^i(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x))\), for \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), are vector spaces of finite rank over \(k(x)\), zero except for a finite number, and the function

\[ x\longmapsto\sum(-1)^i\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^i(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)) \]

is locally constant on \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\).

(ii) If \(E\) is \((p-1)\)-pseudo-coherent, \(H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x))\) is, for \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), a vector space of finite rank over \(k(x)\), and the function

\[ x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)) \]

is upper semi-continuous on \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\). If moreover the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) from \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) to \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) is exact, \(H^p(E)\) is locally free of finite type and the preceding function is locally constant.

(iii) Suppose \(E\) is \(p\)-pseudo-coherent (resp. \((p-1)\)-pseudo-coherent), and let \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\). If the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}M)\) is right exact (resp. left exact) on the category \(\operatorname{Mod}(x)\) of \(\mathcal O_{X,x}\)-Modules, there exists a \(x\)-pointed open object \(U\) of \(X\) such that the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E|U\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) is right exact (resp. left exact) on \(\operatorname{Mod}(U)\).

Proof. (i) By (I 4.19.1), \(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)\) is a perfect complex of \(k(x)\)-modules, hence (I 5.9 and 3.5) the \(H^i(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x))\) are of finite rank over \(k(x)\) and zero except for a finite number. We have

\[ \tag{5.5.1} \operatorname{rg}(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)) =\sum(-1)^i\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^i(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)), \]

as one sees by an immediate dévissage using the additivity of the rank function. Taking (5.4.1 a)) into account, assertion (i) thus follows from the compatibility of the rank with inverse images (I 6.12).

(ii) After truncating and translating, we may, for the first assertion, assume \(E\) strictly perfect, \(p=0\), and \(E^i=0\) for \(i\notin[-1,+1]\). For \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), set \(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)=E_{k(x)}\). By (5.5.1) we have

\[ \operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^0(E_{k(x)}) =\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)}) +\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^1(E_{k(x)}) +\operatorname{rg}(E_x), \]

so it suffices to prove that the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)})\) (resp. \(\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^1(E_{k(x)})\)) is upper semi-continuous (since the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}(E_x)=\operatorname{rg}(E_{k(x)})\) is locally constant). For the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^1(E_{k(x)})\), this is an immediate consequence of (5.4.1 b))(*). For the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)})\), we may assume \(E^1=0\), i.e. replace \(E\) by \(E'=(0\longrightarrow E^{-1}\longrightarrow E^0\longrightarrow0)\). We already know that the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^0(E'_{k(x)})\) is upper semi-continuous, hence so is the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E'_{k(x)})=\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)})\), since the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^0(E'_{k(x)})-\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E'_{k(x)})=\operatorname{rg}(E'_x)\) is locally constant.

Let us now prove the second assertion. After truncating, we may assume \(E\) strictly perfect and \(E^i=0\) for \(i<p-1\). The \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module \(Z'^i(E)=\operatorname{Coker}(E^{i-1}\longrightarrow E^i)\) is therefore of finite presentation. We have an exact sequence:

\[ (*)\qquad 0\longrightarrow H^p(E)\longrightarrow Z'^p(E)\longrightarrow E^{p+1} \longrightarrow Z'^{p+1}(E)\longrightarrow0. \]

Since the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) is right and left exact, \(Z'^{p+1}(E)\) and \(Z'^p(E)\) are flat by (5.2 (iii)), hence (I 5.8.3) locally free of finite type. The exactness of \((*)\) then implies that \(H^p(E)\) is locally free of finite type, and consequently that the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^p(E_{k(x)})=\operatorname{rg}(H^p(E)_x)\)

is locally constant, which completes the proof of (ii).

(iii) We may assume \(E\) strictly perfect and \(E^i=0\) for \(i<p\) (resp. \(p-1\)). To say that the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}M)\) is right exact (resp. left exact) on \(\operatorname{Mod}(x)\) is equivalent, by (5.2 (iii)), to saying that \(Z'^{p+1}(E_x)\) (resp. \(Z'^p(E_x)\)) (with the notations of (ii)) is flat, hence free of finite type (being of finite presentation). Since we have \(Z'^{p+1}(E_x)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}Z'^{p+1}(E)_x\) (resp. \(Z'^p(E_x)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}Z'^p(E)_x\)), the usual argument (cf. EGA \(0_{\mathrm I}\) 5.2.7) shows that there exists a \(x\)-pointed object \(U\) of \(X\) such that \(Z'^{p+1}(E|U)\) (resp. \(Z'^p(E|U)\)) is free of finite type, and we are done.

Corollary 5.6. (EGA III 7.6.9).

Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(p\in\mathbb Z\), and \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\) a \((p-1)\)-pseudo-coherent complex. Then:

(i) For \(x\in X\), \(H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(x))\) is of finite rank over \(k(x)\) and the function

\[ x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(x)) \]

is constructible and upper semi-continuous on \(X\).

(ii) Suppose \(X\) quasi-separated and \(E\) with quasi-coherent and locally bounded cohomology. If the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) is exact on the category of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules, the function \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(x))\) is locally constant and \(H^p(E)\) is locally free of finite type. Conversely, if \(X\) is locally noetherian and reduced and if the preceding function is locally constant, the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) is exact on the category of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules.

Proof. If \(X\) is integral with generic point \(x\), the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}M)\) is exact on the category of \(\mathcal O_{X,x}\)-modules (since \(\mathcal O_{X,x}=k(x)\)), hence (5.5 (iii)), there exists an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\) such that the functor \(M\longmapsto H^p(E|U\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) is exact on \(\operatorname{Mod}(U)\), and, on \(U\), the function

\[ y\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(y)) \]

is locally constant by (5.5 (ii)). The constructibility assertion of (i) follows at once. The other assertions follow from (5.5 (ii) and (iii)) and (5.2 (iv)), except the converse of (ii), for which it suffices, after reducing to \(E\) strictly perfect (after localization and truncation), to apply (EGA III 7.6.2 and 7.6.5) to the functor \(T_{-p}=H^p(E\otimes\,\cdot\,)\).

Proposition 5.7. (EGA III 7.7.5 and 7.9.4).

Let \(f:X\longrightarrow Y\) be a proper morphism of quasi-compact schemes, \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^b(f)_{\mathrm{parf}}\) (4.2), and \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Then, subject to the validity of (2.1), hence for example if \(f\) is projective or if \(Y\) is noetherian:

(i) For \(y\in Y\), the \(H^i(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y))\) are vector spaces of finite rank over \(k(y)\), zero except for a finite number, and the function

\[ y\longmapsto\sum(-1)^i\operatorname{rg}_{k(y)} H^i(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y)) \]

is locally constant on \(Y\).

(ii) The function

\[ y\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(y)} H^p(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y)) \]

is constructible and upper semi-continuous on \(Y\).

(iii) Suppose \(Y\) quasi-separated. Then, if the functor \(M\longmapsto R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) is exact on the category of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Modules, \(R^pf_*(E)\) is a locally free \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Module of finite type, and the function of (ii) is locally constant. Conversely, if \(Y\) is noetherian and reduced, and if the function of (ii) is locally constant, the functor \(M\longmapsto R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) is exact on the category of quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Modules.

Proof. By (4.8), \(Rf_*(E)\) is a perfect complex. Assertion (i) (resp. (ii)) thus follows from (5.5 (i)) (resp. (5.6 (i))). Finally, if \(M\) is a quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Module, the canonical arrow

\[ Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M \longrightarrow Rf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \]

is an isomorphism by (3.7), so assertion (iii) follows from (5.6 (ii)).

Remarks 5.8.

a) In the situation of (5.7), let us denote by \(i_y:X_y\longrightarrow X\) the injection of the fiber of \(X\) above a point \(y\) of \(Y\). One can show (cf. (EGA III 6 and IV 3.1.0)) that for \(f\) flat (resp. \(E\) bounded with quasi-coherent and \(Y\)-flat components) we have the Künneth formula:

\[ H^i(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y)) \mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}H^i(X_y,E_y), \]

where \(E_y=Li_y^*(E)\) (resp. \(i_y^*(E)\)).

b) One can develop for complex analytic spaces an apparatus analogous to that of this section (exchange, semi-continuity and continuity properties)(1). The essential ingredients are: 1) the finiteness theorem for proper morphisms ("Grauert's theorem"); 2) an analogue of the projection formula (3.7), which can be stated as follows: let \(f:X\longrightarrow Y\) be a morphism of analytic spaces, where \(X\) is assumed to be of bounded dimension, and let \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\), \(M\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(Y)_{\mathrm{coh}}\) ("coh" means "with coherent cohomology"). The canonical arrow

\[ Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M \longrightarrow Rf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \]

is an isomorphism (the hypothesis on \(X\) ensures (T.F II 5.12) that \(f_*\) is of finite cohomological dimension, hence that \(Rf_*\) is defined on \(D(X)\)).

Unlike statement 1), statement 2) is essentially trivial, and follows from a dévissage analogous to that of the proof of (3.7); one has moreover more elbow room since \(Rf_*\) is defined on \(D(X)\), in particular no hypothesis on \(E\) is needed (apart from \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\)).

BIBLIOGRAPHY

[1] Grauert, H., Ein Theorem der Analytischen Garbentheorie ..., Pub. IHES, n°5.

[H] Hartshorne, R., Residues and Duality, Lecture Notes n°20, Springer, 1966.

[T.F] Godement, R., Théorie des faisceaux, Hermann, 1958.

Lemma 7.1.

Let \(i:Y\longrightarrow X\) be a regular closed immersion (VII 1.4), of bounded codimension, so that \(i\) is a perfect morphism (VII 1.9), and we can therefore define the morphism (IV 2.12)

\[i^*:K_\bullet(X)\longrightarrow K_\bullet(Y).\]

Let on the other hand \(N\) be the conormal sheaf for \(i\), which is a locally free sheaf of finite type on \(Y\) (VII 1.6), so that we can form

\[\lambda_{-1}(N)\in K'(Y).\]

Consider also the direct image homomorphism (IV 2.11)

\[i_*:K_\bullet(Y)\longrightarrow K_\bullet(X).\]

This being so, we have the formula

\[i^*i_*(x)=x\,\lambda_{-1}(N)\qquad\text{pour }x\in K_\bullet(Y),\]

Lemma 4.3.

Under the conditions of 4.1, let \(L\) be an invertible sheaf on \(Y\) equipped with a gluing datum

\[\varphi:p_1^*L\mathbin{\widetilde\longrightarrow}p_2^*L.\]

For this datum to be effective, it is necessary and sufficient that the five following conditions be satisfied.

1) For every \(i\geq0\), \(R^if_*(L)\) is flat over \(S\).

2) For every \(j\geq0\), \(R^jg_*(p_1^*L)\) is flat over \(S\).

3) The cokernel of \(\pi_1-\pi_2:f_*(L)\longrightarrow g_*(p_1^*L)\mathbin{\widetilde\longrightarrow}g_*(p_2^*(L))\) is flat over \(S\), (where the last isomorphism is \(g_*(\varphi)\)).

4) The kernel \(N\) of \(\pi_1-\pi_2:f_*(L)\longrightarrow g_*(p_1^*L)\) is invertible on \(Y\).

5) The composite morphism \(f^*N\longrightarrow f^*f_*L\longrightarrow L\) is an isomorphism.

Lemma 4.4.

Let \(S\) be a scheme, \(\lambda:X\longrightarrow S\) and \(\mu:Y\longrightarrow S\) proper morphisms of finite presentation, \(f:X\longrightarrow Y\) a \(S\)-morphism. Let \(F\) be a sheaf on \(X\) of finite presentation and flat over \(S\) and, for an integer \(n\), let \(S_n\) be the subfunctor of \(S\) which makes \(R^if_*(F)\) flat over \(S\) for every \(i\geq n\) (precisely, \(S_n(T)=\{\varnothing\}\) if \(R^i(f_T)_*(F_T)\) is flat for every \(i\geq n\), \(S_n(T)=\varnothing\) otherwise). Then \(S_n\longrightarrow S\) is representable by a surjective monomorphism of finite presentation, and then for \(i\geq n\) the \(R^i(f_{S_n})_*(F_{S_n})\) commute with the base changes \(T\longrightarrow S_n\). Moreover \(S_n\) coincides with the functor \(S'_n\) which makes exact the functors

\[M\longmapsto R^i(f_V)_*(F_V\otimes\lambda_V^*M)\qquad\text{pour }i\geq n\]

where \(M\) ranges over the quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_V\)-modules for every affine open subscheme \(V\) of \(S\).

1.12.

Let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme and \(X\) a \(S\)-scheme of finite type. Let \(\mathfrak F\) be a family of classes of coherent sheaves on the fibers of \(X/S\); that is, for every point \(s\in S\) and every extension \(K\) of \(k(s)\), we are given coherent sheaves \(F_K\) on the algebraic scheme \(X_K\), and we say that an \(F_K\) and an \(F'_{K'}\) are in the same class if there exist \(k(s)\)-homomorphisms from \(K,K'\) into a common extension \(K''\) of \(k(s)\) such that \(F_{K''}(=F_K\otimes_K K'')\) and \(F'_{K''}\) are isomorphic over \(X_{K''}\). Then the family \(\mathfrak F\) is said to be limited by the coherent sheaf \(F\) on \(X_T=X\times_S T\) where \(T\) is of finite type over \(S\), if \(\mathfrak F\) is contained in the family of the classes of the sheaves \(F_{k(t)}\), with \(t\in T\); we say that \(\mathfrak F\) is limited if there exists \(T,F\) as above.

Suppose moreover that \(X/S\) is projective and equipped with a (relatively) ample invertible sheaf \(\mathcal O_X(1)\). Then \(\mathfrak F\) is said to be a \((b)\)-family, for a sequence of integers \((b)=(b_0,\dots,b_r)\), if every class in \(\mathfrak F\) is represented by an \(F_K\) with \(K\) algebraically closed, which is a \((b)\)-sheaf.

Theorem 1.13.

Let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme and \(X\) a projective \(S\)-scheme equipped with an ample sheaf \(\mathcal O_X(1)\) whose induced sheaves \(\mathcal O_{X_s}(1)\), with \(s\in S\), are generated by their \(H^0(\mathcal O_{X_s}(1))\); let \(\mathfrak F\) be a family of classes of coherent sheaves on the fibers of \(X/S\). Then the following conditions are equivalent:

(i) \(\mathfrak F\) is limited. Moreover, if all the \(F_K\in\mathfrak F\) are locally free of rank \(p\), then we may assume that \(\mathfrak F\) is limited by a sheaf \(F\) on some \(X_T\), with \(F\) locally free of rank \(p\).

(ii) The set of Hilbert polynomials \(\chi(F_K(n))\) of the \(F_K\in\mathfrak F\) is finite, and there exists a sequence of integers \((b)\) such that \(\mathfrak F\) is a \((b)\)-family.

(iii) The set of Hilbert polynomials \(\chi(F_K(n))\) of the \(F_K\in\mathfrak F\) is finite, and there exists an integer \(m\) such that all the \(F_K\in\mathfrak F\) are \(m\)-regular.

(iv) The set of Hilbert polynomials \(\chi(F_K(n))\) of the \(F_K\in\mathfrak F\) is finite, and \(\mathfrak F\) is contained in the family of the classes of quotients of sheaves of the form \(E_K\), where \(E\) is a coherent sheaf on some \(X_T\). Moreover, we may assume \(T=S\) and \(E\) of the form \(\mathcal O_X(-m)^{\oplus M}\).

\(v\) \(\mathfrak F\) is contained in the family of the classes of cokernels of homomorphisms of the form \(E'_K\to E_K\), where \(E'\) and \(E\) are coherent sheaves on some \(X_T\). Moreover, we may assume \(T=S\) and \(E'\) and \(E\) of the form \(\mathcal O_X(-m')^{\oplus M'}\) and \(\mathcal O_X(-m)^{\oplus M}\).

proposals.before: Remark 5.3. Let \(k\) be an algebraically closed field, and \(X\) a proper and smooth surface over \(k\). Then the second Betti number \(b^2(X)\) can be interpreted as being \(c_2(X)-2+2b^1(X)\), where \(b^1(X)=2\dim(\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k})\), and \(c_2(X)=\) the second Chern class \(=\) the Euler-Poincaré characteristic \(=\) the intersection number of the diagonal of \(X\times X\) with itself; thus \(b^2(X)\) has an interpretation independent of cohomology. 5. Applications : théorèmes d'échange et de semi-continuité(1).

Lemme 5.1.

Soit \((X,\mathcal O_X)\) un topos annelé (commutatif), notons \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) la catégorie des \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules, \(D(X)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(X))\). Soient \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\), et \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Considérons les conditions suivantes :

a) Le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) de \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) dans \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) est exact à droite.

a') La flèche canonique

\[ H^p(E)\otimes M\longrightarrow H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M) \]

est un isomorphisme pour tout \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Mod}(X)\).

b) Le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^{p+1}(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) de \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) dans \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) est exact à gauche.

b') La flèche canonique définie ci-dessous

\[ (*)\qquad H^{p+1}(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(H^{-p-1}(E^\vee),M) \]

est un isomorphisme pour tout \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Mod}(X)\).

Alors on a :

\[ \mathrm{a)}\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{a')} \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{b)}\Longleftarrow\mathrm{b')}. \]

En outre, si \(E\) est pseudo-cohérent, les conditions a), a'), b), b') sont équivalentes.

Définition de \((*)\). La flèche canonique (I 7.5) \(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}E\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X\), où \(E^\vee=\mathbf R\!\operatorname{Hom}(E,\mathcal O_X)\), donne, par tensorisation avec \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Mod}(X)\), une flèche

\[ E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}E \mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M\longrightarrow M, \]

d'où par la formule d'adjonction chère à Cartan (I 7.4), une flèche canonique

\[ (**)\qquad E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M \longrightarrow\mathbf R\!\operatorname{Hom}(E^\vee,M). \]

Composant la flèche induite par \((**)\) sur \(H^{p+1}\) avec la flèche canonique

\[ (***)\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^{p+1}(E^\vee,M) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H^{-p-1}(E^\vee),M), \]

on obtient la flèche \((*)\).

Preuve. Les implications

\[ \mathrm{a')}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{a)} \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm{b)} \Longleftarrow\mathrm{b')} \]

sont triviales. Prouvons a) \(\Longrightarrow\) a'). Soit \(M\) un \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module. Il existe une suite exacte \(M^1\longrightarrow M^0\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow0\), où \(M^0\) et \(M^1\) sont sommes directes de faisceaux du type \(\mathcal O_{U,X}\), où \(U\) est un objet de \(X\). Utilisant l'exactitude à droite et la commutation aux sommes directes des foncteurs \(H^p(E)\otimes\,\cdot\,\) et \(H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}\,\cdot\,)\), on se ramène à prouver que la flèche de a') est un isomorphisme pour \(M=\mathcal O_{U,X}\), \(U\in\operatorname{ob}X\). Or \(H^p(E)\otimes\mathcal O_{U,X}\) (resp. \(H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}\mathcal O_{U,X})\)) s'identifie canoniquement (SGA 4 IV 2.13) à \(i_!(H^p(E)|U)\) (resp. \(H^p(i_!(E|U))\)), où \(i_!\) est le prolongement par \(0\) en dehors de \(U\), et l'on gagne car \(i_!\) est exact.

Supposons \(E\) pseudo-cohérent, et prouvons b) \(\Longrightarrow\) b'). Il suffit évidemment de montrer que \((*)\) est un isomorphisme pour \(M\) injectif. Comme la flèche \((***)\) est un isomorphisme pour \(M\) injectif, l'assertion va donc résulter de la suivante :

(5.1.1) : la flèche \((**)\) est un isomorphisme si \(E\) est pseudo-cohérent et \(M\) injectif.

Preuve de (5.1.1). Notons \(T\) (resp. \(T'\)) le foncteur de \(D^-(X)\) dans \(D(X)\) défini par \(F\longmapsto F\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M\) (resp. \(\mathbf R\!\operatorname{Hom}(F^\vee,M)\)). Soit \(n\in\mathbb Z\) ; si \(H^i(F)=0\) pour \(i>n\), alors \(H^iT(F)=0\) pour \(i>n\), \(H^i(F^\vee)=0\) pour \(i<-n\), et \(H^iT'(F)=0\) pour \(i>n\) si \(M\) est injectif. Comme d'autre part la flèche \((**)\) commute à la restriction à un ouvert, et qu'un injectif restreint à un ouvert est encore injectif, on peut, quitte à se localiser et à tronquer, supposer \(E\) strictement parfait (2.1). Par dévissage, on se ramène alors à \(E=\mathcal O_X\), et l'on gagne.

Remarques 5.2.

(i) La condition a) (resp. a'), b), b')) est de nature locale : si \((X_\alpha)\) est un recouvrement ouvert de l'objet final de \(X\), et si, pour chaque \(\alpha\), la condition a) (resp. ...) est vérifiée pour \(X_\alpha\) et \(E|X_\alpha\), alors a) (resp. ...) est vérifiée.

(ii) Si \(x\) est un point de \(X\), notons \(\mathrm a_x\) (resp. \(\mathrm a'_x\), etc.) la condition a) (resp. a'), etc.) relative à \(E_x\) et \(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{X,x})\). Alors, si \(X\) a assez de points, la condition a) (resp. a'), b)) équivaut à la condition « pour tout point \(x\) de \(X\), \(\mathrm a_x\) (resp. \(\mathrm a'_x\), \(\mathrm b_x\)) », et équivaut à la condition « pour tout point \(x\) de \(X\), \(\mathrm b'_x\) » si \(E\) est pseudo-cohérent ; en outre la condition a') équivaut à la condition analogue où l'on remplace « pour tout \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) » par « pour tout \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module conoyau d'un homomorphisme \(\mathcal O_{U,X}^p\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{U,X}^q\), où \(U\) est un objet de \(X\) ».

(iii) Le critère (EGA III 7.4.2) s'étend mot pour mot à notre situation : si \(E\) est à composantes plates, la condition a) signifie simplement que \(\operatorname{Coker}(E^p\longrightarrow E^{p+1})\) est plat, donc localement facteur direct d'un Module libre de type fini si \(E^p\) et \(E^{p+1}\) sont supposés être en outre de présentation finie (I 5.8.3). On en déduit en particulier que, si \(E\) est parfait, alors \(E\) vérifie la condition a) relative à l'entier \(p\) si et seulement si \(E^\vee\) vérifie la condition a) relative à l'entier \(-p-1\).

(iv) Soient \(X\) un schéma quasi-séparé, \(\mathcal O_X\) le faisceau structural, \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\) un complexe à cohomologie localement bornée et quasi-cohérente. Notons \(\mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\) (resp. \(\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), etc.) la condition analogue à a) (resp. a'), etc.) où l'on remplace \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) par la catégorie \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(X)\) des \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules quasi-cohérents. Alors on a

\[ \mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm b_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftarrow\mathrm b'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}), \]

et les conditions précédentes sont équivalentes si \(E\) est pseudo-cohérent.

En effet, comme \(X\) est quasi-séparé, tout faisceau quasi-cohérent sur un ouvert affine de \(X\) est induit par un faisceau quasi-cohérent sur \(X\) (EGA I 9.4.2 et IV 1.2.7). Il en résulte que la condition \(\mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\) (resp. \(\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), \(\mathrm b_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), \(\mathrm b'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\)) est vérifiée si et seulement si elle l'est au-dessus de tout ouvert affine. Pour prouver les implications ci-dessus, on peut donc supposer \(X\) affine. Alors (II 3.5) \(E\) est isomorphe dans \(D(X)\) à un complexe de Modules quasi-cohérents, et les implications

\[ \mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm b_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \Longleftarrow\mathrm b'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}) \]

résultent de (5.1) appliqué au topos « ponctuel » annelé par \(\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\) ; il en est de même, en vertu de (II 2.2.10 a)), de l'implication \(\mathrm b_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm b'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\) pour \(E\) pseudo-cohérent. Enfin l'équivalence \(\mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), ou, ce qui revient au même, \(\mathrm a')\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\), découle de la dernière remarque de (ii) (et du fait que les faisceaux quasi-cohérents « se prolongent », \(X\) étant quasi-séparé).

Proposition 5.3. (propriété d'échange) (EGA III 7.7.5 II).

Soient \(f:X\longrightarrow Y\) un morphisme de schémas quasi-compacts et quasi-séparés, \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^b(X)\) un complexe à cohomologie quasi-cohérente et d'amplitude plate finie rel. à \(f\), et \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Considérons les conditions suivantes :

a) Le foncteur \(M\longmapsto R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) de \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\)(1) dans \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\)(2) est exact à droite.

a') La flèche canonique

\[ R^pf_*(E)\otimes M\longrightarrow R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \]

(composée de la flèche canonique \(R^pf_*(E)\otimes M\longrightarrow H^p(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) et de l'isomorphisme (3.7) \(H^p(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\)) est un isomorphisme pour tout \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\).

b) Le foncteur \(M\longmapsto R^{p+1}f_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) de \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\) dans \(\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\) est exact à gauche.

b') La flèche canonique

\[ R^{p+1}f_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(H^{-p-1}((Rf_*(E))^\vee),M) \]

(composée de l'isomorphisme (3.7) \(R^{p+1}f_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}H^{p+1}(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) et de la flèche canonique (5.1 \((*)\)) \(H^{p+1}(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H^{-p-1}((Rf_*(E))^\vee),M)\)) est un isomorphisme pour tout \(M\in\operatorname{ob}\operatorname{Qcoh}(Y)\).

c) Pour tout changement de base \(Y'\longrightarrow Y\), la flèche canonique

\[ R^pf_*(E)\otimes_Y\mathcal O_{Y'} \longrightarrow H^p\bigl(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}\mathcal O_{Y'}\bigr) \]

est un isomorphisme.

Alors on a :

\[ \mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a') \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm b) \Longleftrightarrow\mathrm c) \Longleftarrow\mathrm b'). \]

En outre, si \(f\) est propre, \(E\) pseudo-cohérent rel. à \(f\) (donc parfait rel. à \(f\)), et sous réserve de validité de (2.1) pour \(f\) (donc en particulier si \(f\) est projectif ou si \(Y\) est noethérien), les conditions précédentes sont équivalentes.

Preuve. Les implications \(\mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm a')\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm b)\Longleftarrow\mathrm b')\) résultent aussitôt de (3.7), (5.1) et (5.2 (iv)), de même que l'implication \(\mathrm b')\Longleftarrow\mathrm b)\) (pour \(f\) propre et \(E\) pseudo-cohérent rel. à \(f\)) en vertu de (2.1). Il reste à prouver qu'on a \(\mathrm a)\Longleftrightarrow\mathrm c)\). Cela va découler de la première assertion du lemme suivant :

Lemme 5.3.1.

Soit \(X\) un schéma quasi-séparé, et soit \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\) un complexe à cohomologie localement bornée et quasi-cohérente. Alors la condition (5.1 a)) équivaut à la condition

c) Pour tout schéma \(X'\) au-dessus de \(X\), la flèche canonique

\[ H^p(E)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'} \longrightarrow H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'}) \]

est un isomorphisme.

En outre, si \(E\) est pseudo-cohérent, la condition (5.1 a)) implique que, pour tout morphisme \(X'\longrightarrow X\), la flèche canonique

\[ \tag{5.3.1.1} H^{-p-1}(E^\vee)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'} \longrightarrow H^{-p-1}\bigl((E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})^\vee\bigr), \]

composée de \(H^{-p-1}(E^\vee)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'}\longrightarrow H^{-p-1}(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})\) et de la flèche canonique (I 7.1.2) \(H^{-p-1}(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})\longrightarrow H^{-p-1}((E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})^\vee)\), est un isomorphisme.

Preuve. a) \(\Longrightarrow\) c). La question étant locale sur \(X'\), on peut supposer \(X\) (resp. \(X'\)) affine d'anneau \(A\) (resp. \(A'\)). D'après (II 3.5), on peut supposer d'autre part que l'on a \(E=F^\sim\), où \(F\) est un complexe de \(A\)-modules. Par hypothèse (condition a')) la flèche

\[ H^p(F)\otimes_AA'\longrightarrow H^p(F\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_A}A') \]

est un isomorphisme, et l'on gagne puisque \(H^p(E)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'}\) (resp. \(H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})\)) s'identifie canoniquement au faisceau sur \(X'\) défini par le \(A'\)-module \(H^p(F)\otimes_AA'\) (resp. \(H^p(F\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_A}A')\)).

c) \(\Longrightarrow\) a). Compte tenu de (5.2 (iv)), il suffit de prouver c) \(\Longrightarrow\) \(\mathrm a'_{\mathrm{qcoh}}\). La question étant locale (puisque \(X\) est quasi-séparé), on peut supposer \(X\) affine d'anneau \(A\), et \(E=F^\sim\), où \(F\) est un complexe de \(A\)-modules. Soit \(M=N^\sim\) un \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module quasi-cohérent. Il s'agit de montrer que la flèche

\[ H^p(F)\otimes_AN\longrightarrow H^p(F\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_A}N) \]

est un isomorphisme. Mais, si l'on pose \(A'=D_A(N)\) (EGA \(0_{\mathrm{IV}}\) 18.2.3), \(X'=\operatorname{Spec}(A')\), cela résulte de c) appliquée au morphisme canonique \(X'\longrightarrow X\).

Prouvons la dernière assertion. La question étant locale sur \(X'\), on peut, d'après (II 2.2.10 b)), supposer \(E\) strictement pseudo-cohérent. De plus, l'assertion ne faisant intervenir qu'une partie de longueur bornée de \(E\), on peut, quitte à tronquer, supposer \(E\) strictement parfait. Alors \((E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'})^\vee\) s'identifie canoniquement (I 7.1.2) à \(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'}\), et la flèche (5.3.1.1) peut être récrite comme la flèche canonique

\[ (*)\qquad H^{-p-1}(E^\vee)\otimes_X\mathcal O_{X'} \longrightarrow H^{-p-1}(E^\vee\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}\mathcal O_{X'}). \]

Si \(E\) vérifie la condition (5.1 a)) pour l'entier \(p\), \(E^\vee\) vérifie la même condition pour l'entier \(-p-1\) en vertu de (5.2 (iii)), et la flèche \((*)\) est un isomorphisme, d'après la première assertion de (5.3.1). Ceci achève la démonstration de (5.3.1), et par suite de (5.3).

Remarque 5.3.2.

La proposition (5.3) s'applique en particulier lorsque \(E\) est un complexe à degrés bornés de \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules quasi-cohérents plats et de présentation finie rel. à \(f\) : en effet, \(E\) est alors d'amplitude parfaite finie rel. à \(f\) en vertu de (4.3.2).

Définition 5.4.

Soit \(X\) un topos, notons \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\) l'ensemble de ses points (SGA 4 IV 6.1). Soient \(M\) un ensemble ordonné, \(f:\operatorname{Pt}(X)\longrightarrow M\) une application, et \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\). On dit que \(f\) est semi-continue supérieurement (resp. semi-continue inférieurement, resp. localement constante) en \(x\) s'il existe un objet \(x\)-ponctué \(U\) de \(X\) tel que pour tout point \(y\) de \(U\) on ait \(f(y)\leq f(x)\) (resp. \(f(y)\geq f(x)\), resp. \(f(y)=f(x)\)). On dit que \(f\) est semi-continue supérieurement (resp. semi-continue inférieurement, resp. localement constante) si elle l'est en tout point(1).

Exemples 5.4.1.

a) Notons \(M_X\) le faisceau constant de valeur \(M\) sur \(X\), et soit \(s\in H^0(X,M)\). L'application \(x\longmapsto s(x)=x^*(s)\) de \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\) dans \(M\) est localement constante. En particulier, soit \(E\) un complexe parfait sur \(X\) supposé localement annelé : le rang de \(E\) (I 6.11) définit une fonction localement constante sur \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\) à valeurs dans \(\mathbb Z\).

b) Supposons \(X\) localement annelé, et soit \(P\) un \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module de type fini. Pour \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), notons \(\mathcal O_{X,x}\) l'anneau local fibre de \(\mathcal O_X\) en \(x\), et \(k(x)\) le corps résiduel. Alors, pour \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), \(P_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}k(x)\) est de rang fini sur \(k(x)\), et la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}(P_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}k(x))\) est semi-continue supérieurement. En effet, si, pour \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), \(P_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}k(x)\) est de rang \(n\), il existe un épimorphisme \(\mathcal O_{X,x}^n\longrightarrow P_x\) d'après Nakayama, et, comme \(P\) est de type fini, il existe un objet \(x\)-ponctué \(U\) de \(X\) et un épimorphisme \(\mathcal O_U^n\longrightarrow P|U\), d'où l'assertion.

Lemme 5.5.

Soient \((X,\mathcal O_X)\) un topos localement annelé, \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\), et \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Alors on a, avec les notations de (5.4.1 b)) :

(i) Si \(E\) est parfait, les \(H^i(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x))\), pour \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), sont des espaces vectoriels de rang fini sur \(k(x)\), nuls sauf un nombre fini, et la fonction

\[ x\longmapsto\sum(-1)^i\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^i(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)) \]

est localement constante sur \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\).

(ii) Si \(E\) est \((p-1)\)-pseudo-cohérent, \(H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x))\) est, pour \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), un espace vectoriel de rang fini sur \(k(x)\), et la fonction

\[ x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)) \]

est semi-continue supérieurement sur \(\operatorname{Pt}(X)\). Si en outre le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) de \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) dans \(\operatorname{Mod}(X)\) est exact, \(H^p(E)\) est localement libre de type fini et la fonction précédente est localement constante.

(iii) Supposons \(E\) \(p\)-pseudo-cohérent (resp. \((p-1)\)-pseudo-cohérent), et soit \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\). Si le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}M)\) est exact à droite (resp. à gauche) sur la catégorie \(\operatorname{Mod}(x)\) des \(\mathcal O_{X,x}\)-Modules, il existe un ouvert \(x\)-ponctué \(U\) de \(X\) tel que le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E|U\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) soit exact à droite (resp. à gauche) sur \(\operatorname{Mod}(U)\).

Preuve. (i) D'après (I 4.19.1), \(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)\) est un complexe parfait de \(k(x)\)-modules, donc (I 5.9 et 3.5) les \(H^i(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x))\) sont de rang fini sur \(k(x)\) et nuls sauf un nombre fini. On a

\[ \tag{5.5.1} \operatorname{rg}(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)) =\sum(-1)^i\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^i(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)), \]

comme on le voit par un dévissage immédiat utilisant l'additivité de la fonction rang. Compte tenu de (5.4.1 a)), l'assertion (i) résulte donc de la compatibilité du rang avec les images inverses (I 6.12).

(ii) Quitte à tronquer et à translater, on peut, pour la première assertion, supposer \(E\) strictement parfait, \(p=0\), et \(E^i=0\) pour \(i\notin[-1,+1]\). Pour \(x\in\operatorname{Pt}(X)\), posons \(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}k(x)=E_{k(x)}\). On a d'après (5.5.1)

\[ \operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^0(E_{k(x)}) =\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)}) +\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^1(E_{k(x)}) +\operatorname{rg}(E_x), \]

donc il suffit de prouver que la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)})\) (resp. \(\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^1(E_{k(x)})\)) est semi-continue supérieurement (puisque la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}(E_x)=\operatorname{rg}(E_{k(x)})\) est localement constante). Pour la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^1(E_{k(x)})\), c'est une conséquence immédiate de (5.4.1 b))(*). Pour la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)})\), on peut supposer \(E^1=0\), i.e. remplacer \(E\) par \(E'=(0\longrightarrow E^{-1}\longrightarrow E^0\longrightarrow0)\). On sait déjà que la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^0(E'_{k(x)})\) est semi-continue supérieurement, donc il en est de même de la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E'_{k(x)})=\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E_{k(x)})\), puisque la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^0(E'_{k(x)})-\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^{-1}(E'_{k(x)})=\operatorname{rg}(E'_x)\) est localement constante.

Prouvons maintenant la seconde assertion. Quitte à tronquer, on peut supposer \(E\) strictement parfait et \(E^i=0\) pour \(i<p-1\). Le \(\mathcal O_X\)-Module \(Z'^i(E)=\operatorname{Coker}(E^{i-1}\longrightarrow E^i)\) est donc de présentation finie. On a une suite exacte :

\[ (*)\qquad 0\longrightarrow H^p(E)\longrightarrow Z'^p(E)\longrightarrow E^{p+1} \longrightarrow Z'^{p+1}(E)\longrightarrow0. \]

Comme le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) est exact à droite et à gauche, \(Z'^{p+1}(E)\) et \(Z'^p(E)\) sont plats d'après (5.2 (iii)), donc (I 5.8.3) localement libres de type fini. L'exactitude de \((*)\) implique alors que \(H^p(E)\) est localement libre de type fini, et par suite que la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^p(E_{k(x)})=\operatorname{rg}(H^p(E)_x)\)

est localement constante, ce qui achève la preuve de (ii).

(iii) On peut supposer \(E\) strictement parfait et \(E^i=0\) pour \(i<p\) (resp. \(p-1\)). Dire que le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}M)\) est exact à droite (resp. à gauche) sur \(\operatorname{Mod}(x)\) équivaut, d'après (5.2 (iii)), à dire que \(Z'^{p+1}(E_x)\) (resp. \(Z'^p(E_x)\)) (avec les notations de (ii)) est plat, donc libre de type fini (puisque de présentation finie). Comme on a \(Z'^{p+1}(E_x)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}Z'^{p+1}(E)_x\) (resp. \(Z'^p(E_x)\mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}Z'^p(E)_x\)), l'argument habituel (cf. EGA \(0_{\mathrm I}\) 5.2.7) montre qu'il existe un objet \(x\)-ponctué \(U\) de \(X\) tel que \(Z'^{p+1}(E|U)\) (resp. \(Z'^p(E|U)\)) soit libre de type fini, et l'on gagne.

Corollaire 5.6. (EGA III 7.6.9).

Soient \(X\) un schéma, \(p\in\mathbb Z\), et \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\) un complexe \((p-1)\)-pseudo-cohérent. Alors :

(i) Pour \(x\in X\), \(H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(x))\) est de rang fini sur \(k(x)\) et la fonction

\[ x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(x)) \]

est constructible et semi-continue supérieurement sur \(X\).

(ii) Supposons \(X\) quasi-séparé et \(E\) à cohomologie quasi-cohérente et localement bornée. Si le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) est exact sur la catégorie des \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules quasi-cohérents, la fonction \(x\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)}H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(x))\) est localement constante et \(H^p(E)\) est localement libre de type fini. Inversement, si \(X\) est localement noethérien et réduit et si la fonction précédente est localement constante, le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) est exact sur la catégorie des \(\mathcal O_X\)-Modules quasi-cohérents.

Preuve. Si \(X\) est intègre de point générique \(x\), le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E_x\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}}M)\) est exact sur la catégorie des \(\mathcal O_{X,x}\)-modules (puisque \(\mathcal O_{X,x}=k(x)\)), donc (5.5 (iii)), il existe un voisinage ouvert \(U\) de \(x\) tel que le foncteur \(M\longmapsto H^p(E|U\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M)\) soit exact sur \(\operatorname{Mod}(U)\), et, sur \(U\), la fonction

\[ y\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(x)} H^p(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_X}k(y)) \]

est localement constante d'après (5.5 (ii)). L'assertion de constructibilité de (i) s'en déduit aussitôt. Les autres assertions découlent de (5.5 (ii) et (iii)) et (5.2 (iv)), sauf la réciproque de (ii), pour laquelle il suffit, après s'être ramené à \(E\) strictement parfait (après localisation et troncation), d'appliquer (EGA III 7.6.2 et 7.6.5) au foncteur \(T_{-p}=H^p(E\otimes\,\cdot\,)\).

Proposition 5.7. (EGA III 7.7.5 et 7.9.4).

Soient \(f:X\longrightarrow Y\) un morphisme propre de schémas quasi-compacts, \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^b(f)_{\mathrm{parf}}\) (4.2), et \(p\in\mathbb Z\). Alors, sous réserve de validité de (2.1), donc par exemple si \(f\) est projectif ou si \(Y\) est noethérien :

(i) Pour \(y\in Y\), les \(H^i(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y))\) sont des espaces vectoriels de rang fini sur \(k(y)\), nuls sauf un nombre fini, et la fonction

\[ y\longmapsto\sum(-1)^i\operatorname{rg}_{k(y)} H^i(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y)) \]

est localement constante sur \(Y\).

(ii) La fonction

\[ y\longmapsto\operatorname{rg}_{k(y)} H^p(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y)) \]

est constructible et semi-continue supérieurement sur \(Y\).

(iii) Supposons \(Y\) quasi-séparé. Alors, si le foncteur \(M\longmapsto R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) est exact sur la catégorie des \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Modules quasi-cohérents, \(R^pf_*(E)\) est un \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Module localement libre de type fini, et la fonction de (ii) est localement constante. Inversement, si \(Y\) est noethérien et réduit, et si la fonction de (ii) est localement constante, le foncteur \(M\longmapsto R^pf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M)\) est exact sur la catégorie des \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Modules quasi-cohérents.

Preuve. D'après (4.8), \(Rf_*(E)\) est un complexe parfait. L'assertion (i) (resp. (ii)) résulte donc de (5.5 (i)) (resp. (5.6 (i))). Enfin, si \(M\) est un \(\mathcal O_Y\)-Module quasi-cohérent, la flèche canonique

\[ Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M \longrightarrow Rf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \]

est un isomorphisme d'après (3.7), donc l'assertion (iii) résulte de (5.6 (ii)).

Remarques 5.8.

a) Dans la situation de (5.7), notons \(i_y:X_y\longrightarrow X\) l'injection de la fibre de \(X\) au-dessus d'un point \(y\) de \(Y\). On peut montrer (cf. (EGA III 6 et IV 3.1.0)) que pour \(f\) plat (resp. \(E\) borné à composantes quasi-cohérentes et \(Y\)-plates) on a la formule de Künneth :

\[ H^i(Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}k(y)) \mathrel{\widetilde\longrightarrow}H^i(X_y,E_y), \]

où \(E_y=Li_y^*(E)\) (resp. \(i_y^*(E)\)).

b) On peut développer pour les espaces analytiques complexes un tapis analogue à celui de ce numéro (propriétés d'échange, de semi-continuité, de continuité)(1). Les ingrédients essentiels sont : 1) le théorème de finitude pour les morphismes propres (« théorème de Grauert ») ; 2) un analogue de la formule de projection (3.7), qu'on peut énoncer ainsi : soit \(f:X\longrightarrow Y\) un morphisme d'espaces analytiques, où \(X\) est supposé de dimension majorée, et soient \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\), \(M\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(Y)_{\mathrm{coh}}\) (« coh » signifie « à cohomologie cohérente »). La flèche canonique

\[ Rf_*(E)\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}}M \longrightarrow Rf_*(E\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}^{\mathbf L}_Y}M) \]

est un isomorphisme (l'hypothèse sur \(X\) assure (T.F II 5.12) que \(f_*\) est de dimension cohomologique finie, donc que \(Rf_*\) est défini sur \(D(X)\)).

À la différence de l'énoncé 1), l'énoncé 2) est essentiellement trivial, et résulte d'un dévissage analogue à celui de la preuve de (3.7) ; on a d'ailleurs les coudées plus franches puisque \(Rf_*\) est défini sur \(D(X)\), en particulier il n'est besoin d'aucune hypothèse sur \(E\) (en dehors de \(E\in\operatorname{ob}D^-(X)\)).
